about: Judge calibration registry (RIMMANDRAKE_SEED_JUDGE_CALIBRATION_FROM_CORPORA; spec design/specs/2026-11-12-refusal-contract-for-judges-and-gates.md section 5). Keyed by family; `hash` is refusal_contract.brief_hash of `brief`. Only a CALIBRATED brief's verdict, either way, has a consequence (a refusal sends work back, a pass signs); any edit to a brief file resets it to UNTESTED (refusal_contract.py calibrate). A brief is CALIBRATED only by a check on its current hash whose case results show every `planted` case ran and came out as planted, good and bad both (refusal_contract.judge_cases; RIMMANDRAKE_EARN_CALIBRATION_BOTH_WAYS): `free_check` is deterministic and runs on every calibrate, `model_check` spends and runs only on `calibrate --model <family>`. `cases` is prose about the corpora a row was seeded from.

proposals: Plant sprites: add an alpha floor to the art pipeline that clears pixels under about alpha 8 before judging. single.png carries about 880 pixels at alpha 1-29 spread to the canvas edges (the alpha bbox is the full 256 width while the opaque bbox is cols 16-239). These pixels are invisible now, but they could show as a faint haze under some shaders or after a down-scale, and they make the bbox-based footprint checks (D3) read the canvas edge instead of the plant.

verdicts.notes: Candidate B, not owner-kept (subject.json), so E3 does not apply. Painterly deep-green fern with pale rachises, fronds swept to one side, which matches the description's 'every frond swept to the cold side as if combed'. No drawn outline (B1a). Real alpha: corners are alpha 0, with no backdrop, halo, ground shadow or stone prop (D4). Measured: opaque bbox rows 23-234, cols 16-239 of 256; about 880 near-invisible pixels at alpha 1-29 spread across the canvas, of which the edge strips are alpha 1 at most, too faint to read as a halo. Canvas is 256 px for drawSize 1, which is generous (D2). In scale.png at 256 px/cell the fern sits inside its own cell at about 0.6 cell, consistent with visualSizeRange.max 0.7, so it neither overflows nor floats (D3). Play zoom (playzoom_single.png and scale.png 32/cell panel): reads as a few bold green frond shapes, clearly apart from the brown ground, so no grey mud (B2). Plants have one picture, so the facing clauses (C) and the pawn clause (F) do not apply. No canon entry, sibling keeps, donor art or owner notes are on record.

proposals: Invented (non-canon) subjects have no appearance target: section A covers only Star Wars canon entries. RM_Huldu's description asks for 'velvet-skinned', 'dorsal comb folded flat like wet fur', and south.png/east.png show a plain Earth otter with no comb visible on east. Proposal: for invented subjects, the description's concrete visual nouns become Must-show checks, sourced to the owner if he agrees.

east.png draws the swimmer standing upright on its hind legs with its forepaws raised, a begging pose rather than a walking or swimming pose. Proposal: a creature's east facing shows its ordinary locomotion stance, because the facing is drawn on every move it makes.
In south.png the tail rises behind the head. At 32 px/cell (playzoom_south.png) the tail reads as a dark spike above the face. This is advisory only, and no constraint covers it.
